class.name: SceneManager
class.brief_description: Engine singleton for Creation-Engine-style scene travel.
class.description:
[SceneManager] loads whole scenes one at a time. [method travel_to] async-loads the target scene behind a loading screen ([SceneTransition]), swaps it in as [member SceneTree.current_scene], then reports a spawn transform so the game's master node can move the player. It is always available in GDScript as [code]SceneManager[/code]. Typical setup, from an autoload's [code]_ready()[/code]: [codeblock] SceneManager.set_catalog_path("res://data/scene_catalog.tres") SceneManager.set_loading_screen("res://ui/loading_screen.tscn") SceneManager.connect("player_spawn_requested", self, "_on_player_spawn")
func _on_player_spawn(xform, spawn_id): $Player.global_transform = xform $Player/Camera.current = true [/codeblock] The scene is pumped from a [SceneTree] idle callback, so loading never blocks a frame for long; raise [member max_polls_per_frame] to load faster, lower it to keep frames smoother.

method.name: bootstrap
method.description: Forces creation of the runtime [SceneTransition] now. Optional — [method travel_to] does this automatically.

method.name: can_travel_back
method.description: True if the travel history is non-empty.

method.name: get_current_scene_id
method.description: Catalog id of the scene currently loaded, or [code]""[/code] before the first travel.

method.name: get_progress
method.description: Load progress of the in-flight travel, [code]0..1[/code].

method.name: reload_current
method.description: Travels to the current scene again, reusing the last spawn id. Does not push history.

method.name: set_catalog_path
method.description: Loads a [SceneCatalog] [code].tres[/code] from this path and uses it.

method.name: set_loading_screen
method.description: [code]res://[/code] path to the loading-screen scene shown during a travel. Its root may implement [code]set_progress(ratio: float)[/code] to drive a bar. Empty falls back to a plain colour fade.

method.name: set_player_target
method.description: After each load, if a node exists at [code]path[/code] and has this method, the manager calls [code]method(transform, spawn_id)[/code] on it — an alternative to connecting [signal player_spawn_requested]. Defaults to [code]/root/GameMaster[/code] and [code]place_player[/code].

method.name: travel_back
method.description: Pops the travel history and returns to the previous scene (at its default spawn).

method.name: travel_to
method.description: Begins travelling to the catalog scene [code]scene_id[/code]. The player is placed at the [SceneSpawnPoint] whose [member SceneSpawnPoint.spawn_id] matches [code]spawn_id[/code] (or the entry's [member SceneCatalogEntry.default_spawn]). Ignored if a travel is already in flight.

members.member: The active [SceneCatalog]. Also settable by path with [method set_catalog_path].
[code]res://[/code] path to the loading-screen scene. Empty falls back to a colour fade.
How many resource-load steps to run per frame while travelling. Higher loads faster but can hitch.

signal.name: travel_started
signal.description: Emitted when [method travel_to] accepts a request and the loading screen begins to show.

signal.name: scene_instanced
signal.description: Emitted right after the new scene becomes the current scene, before the player is placed.

signal.name: player_spawn_requested
signal.description: Emitted with the global transform the player should be moved to. Connect this from the node that owns the player.

signal.name: travel_finished
signal.description: Emitted once the player has been placed and the loading screen begins to hide.

signal.name: travel_failed
signal.description: Emitted when a travel could not start or complete. The previous scene is left untouched.
